root_cause.text: The cpu_id attribute from user space was not validated against nr_cpu_ids before being passed to cpumask_test_cpu(), allowing an out-of-bounds read of the cpumask bitmap.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (dmah->cpu_id >= nr_cpu_ids) { ret = -EINVAL; goto err; }` before `cpumask_test_cpu(dmah->cpu_id, current->cpus_ptr)`. The commit message explicitly states that "cpu_id ... is passed directly to cpumask_test_cpu() without first verifying that the value is within the valid CPU range" and that this can lead to an out-of-bounds read.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check on cpu_id before using it in cpumask operations to enforce valid CPU ID range and avoid potential out-of-bounds access.
intent_record.what: Added a new if statement to check if dmah->cpu_id is >= nr_cpu_ids, returning -EINVAL and jumping to err if true.
intent_record.how: This change prevents the subsequent cpumask_test_cpu call from accessing an out-of-bounds cpu_id, which could cause undefined behavior or a kernel crash. It returns an error early if the cpu_id is invalid.
